source.title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
source.authors: Alexander Stern; Tim Rocktäschel; Acyr F. Locatelli; L. Ruis

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps compute and fits held-out FineWeb loss against compute using power laws, a conceptual test of loss scaling. It does not reproduce the original scaling-law experiments across parameters, tokens, and compute independently.
record.gate_note: The data-unconstrained compute sweep and its fitted loss-versus-compute power laws bear on V1. The study also evaluates downstream benchmarks, but does not fit or test a downstream prediction relationship. Its initialization comparisons concern PPT gains rather than the scaling-law versions.
record.test_reason: In a NanoChat/Muon/FineWeb setting, the study searches for compute-optimal baseline models at 1e18, 3e18 and 9e18 FLOPs. It fits BPB = A·C^-α, giving α=0.0522±0.0003. This is a narrow-range result bearing on V1. It also reports searched optima of about 4.6 tokens per parameter, against Chinchilla's 20, and attributes the gap to data, architecture and optimizer. That bears on V7. Most of the study compares its own PPT curricula against the baseline; those comparisons are not tests of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find no PPT method with a lower multiplicative constant or a significantly larger exponent than the baseline. Synthetic PPT stays above the baseline at every budget, while the C4 control matches it. They do not fit an irreducible-loss term because they have only three budgets. They conclude these recipes would not overtake natural-language training at larger scales.
record.recipe_differences: This is a compute-optimal sweep with a least-squares fit of BPB against compute for separate training curricula, rather than the original scaling-law experiments varying parameters, tokens, and compute. The data-unconstrained sweep uses three compute budgets and does not fit an irreducible-loss term.
record.method_sensitivity: The tested PPT share (1% versus 5%) changes the fitted multiplicative constant; the authors report that the effect on the exponent is unclear. They also report that the PPT methods remain above the baseline at all tested budgets, while C4 matches it.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted loss-vs-compute exponents for synthetic and code PPT curricula (1% and 5%) are within standard error of, or below, the baseline's 0.0522. PPT raises the constant A, and the C4 control matches the baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Front-loaded synthetic pre-pretraining shifts the loss-compute curve up without increasing its scaling exponent.

record.code_released: not stated (Appendix F names the repositories rethinking-ppt and llmtuna-hpo but provides no URL)
record.problems: Only three compute budgets were tested, and the authors do not fit an irreducible-loss term. The over-Chinchilla runs use a reduced hyperparameter sweep, but that setting is not the basis for the Figure 9 scaling fit. Fit values are shown in a figure with an embedded table.

untested.parts: Independent scaling in parameters or in tokens; ranges of several orders of magnitude (only 1e18–9e18 FLOPs); any goodness-of-fit check or comparison against alternative curve forms.
No fitted law is checked against larger runs. The 2.7e19 and over-Chinchilla runs are not compared with the predicted values.
Compute-optimal model sizes are searched per budget (baseline depth 12/16/20), but no allocation exponent for parameters or tokens is fitted.
Only depth is searched, and width is tied to depth (64d). No shape ablation at fixed parameter count.
DCLM CORE and BLiMP are reported per budget, but no fit of downstream score against scale or loss is made.

missing.what: Compute-optimal tokens-per-parameter ratio of about 4.6 at the baseline's searched optima, versus Chinchilla's 20, attributed to data, architecture and optimizer.
Searched compute-optimal model sizes per budget: 179–186M at 1e18, 252–336M at 3e18, 438–561M at 9e18; baseline depths 12, 16 and 20.

record.verdict_notes: The power law is used mainly as a tool to compare curricula. Its bearing on V1 is weak: three points, less than one decade, no test of fit form. The reader's single V1 label lumping all 50 rows was replaced: the PPT rows are method comparisons. Baseline DCLM CORE rises 0.088→0.121→0.165 across budgets, but no downstream predictability fit is attempted.

versions.untested_parts: Tests held-out FineWeb BPB against compute in a data-unconstrained, compute-optimal sweep. Does not independently vary parameter count or training tokens, or test the full several-orders-of-magnitude range.

relationships.condition: Compute-optimal NanoChat baseline, FineWeb BPB, 1e18–9e18 FLOPs, three seeds per budget
relationships.reason: Baseline BPB falls 0.9794→0.9234→0.8733, and the power-law fit gives α=0.0522±0.0003 with small errors (bp-base-1e18, bp-base-3e18, bp-base-9e18, fit-base). The range is under one decade.
relationships.display_finding: BPB falls from 0.9794 through 0.9234 to 0.8733, with fitted exponent 0.0522±0.0003 over less than one decade of compute.

relationships.reason: Based on the text (no row). Appendix D.6 reports about 4.6 tokens per parameter at the searched optima, well below Hoffmann's 20, and attributes this to data, architecture and optimizer.
relationships.display_finding: Searched optima at 1e18–9e18 FLOPs used about 4.6 tokens per parameter versus the reference 20, a difference attributed to data, architecture, and optimizer.
